messages.content: Write the introduction to a public product roadmap for a developer tools company. Around 200 words.

output:
Here's the draft. I've left `[Company]` as a swap-in, and bracketed the two numbers you'd replace with your real ones.

---

## What we're building next

This page is the honest version.

For the last two years we shipped in the dark and told you about it afterward. That worked when there were [400] of you. It doesn't work now — teams are betting release processes on our CLI, and they need to know six months out whether we're going to support the thing they're about to depend on. So we're opening the board.

Three columns: shipping now, next two quarters, and things we've argued about internally without deciding. That third column is the useful one. It's where you'll find remote build caching, the Windows runner, and the plugin API we keep half-designing and shelving. Nothing there is a promise. It's a list of what has our attention.

We update this monthly, on the first Tuesday, and we move items backward as well as forward. When something slips, the card says why. When we kill a feature, it stays on the page with a note, because a dead feature you can read about is more useful than one that quietly disappears.

Comment on any card. We read them before planning.

---

~205 words. If you'd rather it be less blunt about past opacity, say the word and I'll retune the register — that opening paragraph is the load-bearing choice here.
